title: Img
description: A plain gets loading help: placeholder shows while the real image loads, fallback replaces it if it fails, aspectRatio reserves its box so the page does not jump, and zoomable opens it full-size on click.

placeholder.description: Image shown while the real `src` loads. Replaced the moment the real image decodes.

fallback.description: Image swapped in when `src` fails to load. Without one a broken image raises a loggable error and leaves the element empty.

aspectRatio.description: A CSS aspect ratio (e.g. `16/9`) applied to the element, with `object-fit: cover`. Reserves the box before the image arrives, so the page does not jump as it loads.

lazy.description: Sets `loading="lazy"`, so the browser defers fetching until the image nears the viewport. Bare attribute.
lazy.demoNote: Nothing changes in this box: it is already in view, so the image loads at once. To see the wait, open your browser's Network panel on a long page and scroll down to the image.
lazy.visualReason: Sets loading="lazy", which defers the fetch until the image nears the viewport; the image on screen is unchanged.

zoomable.description: Clicking the image opens it full-size in a lightbox. Bare attribute.

width.description: Width in pixels (the native attribute). On its own the height follows the photo's shape. With `height`, the two numbers set the shape too: the image is cropped to it (`object-fit: cover`), never stretched. It still shrinks to fit a narrower container and keeps that shape.

height.description: Height in pixels (the native attribute). Takes effect only together with `width`: the pair sets the image's shape and the image is cropped to it. On its own it is overridden by the site's `img { height: auto }`. An explicit `aspectRatio` wins over the pair.
